subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In geology, a mineral is a naturally occurring solid substance with a specific chemical composition and crystal structure.
• Minerals are commonly classified using the Dana classification system.
• The system groups minerals based on their chemical composition and crystal structure.
• Quartz (silicon dioxide) is classified as a tectosilicate because of its framework of silicon-oxygen tetrahedra.
• Pyrite (iron sulfide) is classified as a sulfide mineral because it contains sulfur bonded to a metal.
• This classification system was developed by American geologist James Dwight Dana (1813–1895).
prompt: The student wants to provide an example of a mineral. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Minerals are naturally occurring solid substances with specific chemical compositions and crystal structures.
choices.B: One type of mineral is quartz, which is classified as a tectosilicate because of its framework of silicon-oxygen tetrahedra.
choices.C: The Dana classification system groups minerals based on chemical composition and crystal structure and was developed by James Dwight Dana.
choices.D: Minerals are commonly classified using a system that groups them based on their chemical composition and crystal structure.

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer. The sentence provides an example of a mineral: quartz, which is classified as a tectosilicate.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect. The sentence provides a general definition of minerals; it doesn't provide an example of a specific mineral.
